summary: Choose an intentional image-grid and detail hierarchy so pixel structure supports the scene instead of making controls unreadable.
objective: Important objects remain identifiable during camera motion and selection feedback does not disappear into the coarse image.
intent_signals: Keep scene landmarks readable in a coarse image
example_prompts: Make a retro low-resolution maze whose exit, player marker and controls remain clear.

principles: Choose an intentional image-grid and detail hierarchy so pixel structure supports the scene instead of making controls unreadable.
implementation: Use clear silhouettes and large landmarks; keep tiny surface features subordinate to what survives the target image size.
Try a constrained palette and broad light shapes; decide deliberately whether texture pixels and output pixels share the same visual rhythm.
Use measured camera moves and inspect motion at output size; render labels and controls at a readable resolution independent of the stylized scene if needed.

Render at 320x240 (426x240 for 16:9) into a WebGLRenderTarget with NearestFilter and no mipmaps, then upscale to the canvas with integer scaling; keep the HUD, labels and selection outline on a separate full-resolution CSS2D layer.

Cap textures at 128x128 with a 16-colour palette and quantise vertex positions to a 1/16 m grid in the vertex shader for the period wobble; leave collision and picking geometry unquantised so controls stay accurate.
observable_checks: Important objects remain identifiable during camera motion and selection feedback does not disappear into the coarse image.

defaults.rationale: The look lives in the sampling grid rather than in the shading, so the numbers here are chosen for what survives four pixels: a six-hue palette, a three-step value ramp and a key:fill near 2.5:1 that never lets a face go fully black. Neutral tone mapping at exposure 1.0 and bloom at zero are deliberate, because a filmic curve and a bloom halo reintroduce exactly the smooth highlight roll-off the period hardware could not produce.

values.value_structure: 50/35/15 dark/mid/light; three luminance steps per material so the coarse grid reads as bands rather than as noise
values.saturation_rule: six hues maximum; non-focal surfaces <= 55% HSL saturation, the interactive marker is the only element above 75%

lights.ratio: key:fill ~ 2.5:1; a test sphere must show exactly three distinct shading steps and no fully black face

values.intensity_unit: three-intensity (lux-scaled for Directional/Hemisphere, candela for Point/Spot; tuned with the stated tone_mapping.exposure)

materials.notes: MeshLambertMaterial or vertex-lit MeshBasicMaterial; texture magFilter and minFilter NearestFilter, generateMipmaps false, textures 64x64-128x128 on 16-colour palettes; blob shadow decals instead of shadow maps

values.signature_technique: render the scene into a 320x240 nearest-filtered target and upscale by an integer factor, with a 4x4 ordered dither on the colour ramp and affine (non-perspective-correct) UV interpolation on large ground planes
never: a 16-bit gradient across a large sky
text or controls rendered inside the 320x240 buffer

known_limits: Values are authored starting points tuned for Neutral tone mapping at exposure 1.0; re-tune every intensity, fog density and bloom threshold if you change the tone mapping or exposure.
No renderer run for this record; values are authored starting points.
creative_affordances: Combine with voxel or low-poly geometry; retro styling does not mandate a specific historical console or its technical limits.
